codeReview.summary: The README.md (547 lines) was created at the repo root and accurately documents all 8 required content areas. Content was verified against the actual source files: all REST endpoints, request/response DTOs, status codes, WebSocket schema, budget alert rules, and OAuth configuration steps are accurate. Two non-blocking gaps exist: (1) the 'Project Overview' is present as the document intro rather than a named '## Project Overview' section, so the ToC lists only 7 entries; (2) the GET response bodies for /api/categories and /api/transactions are not explicitly documented (only POST response shapes are shown, from which GET responses can be inferred). All existing backend (168) and frontend (136) tests remain passing, as verified by the worker.

issues.description: No dedicated '## Project Overview' heading with its own Table of Contents entry. The project overview content (description + key features) is present at the top of the document as the intro, but the ToC lists only 7 sections (omitting 'Project Overview'). The feature required 8 named sections. Content is present but structure is slightly non-conforming.

GET /api/categories response format not explicitly documented. The section jumps from the endpoint table directly into POST request/response examples. GET returns a JSON array of CategoryResponse objects (same shape as POST 201 response). A reader can infer this from context but it is not stated.

GET /api/transactions response format not explicitly documented. After documenting query parameters and a usage example, the section moves straight to POST request. GET returns a JSON array of TransactionResponse objects. Same shape as POST 201 response but not stated for GET.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The fullstack-worker skill prescribes TDD steps (write failing tests first) and agent-browser end-to-end verification as mandatory procedure. For documentation-only features these steps are inapplicable. The worker correctly skipped them and flagged this in skillFeedback.suggestedChanges, but followedProcedure was marked true — indicating the skill has no conditional path for doc-only work. Adding a note to the skill about how to handle doc-only features (skip TDD, skip agent-browser) would prevent future workers from being confused or wastefully attempting those steps.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Handoff skillFeedback.suggestedChanges: 'For documentation-only features, the fullstack-worker skill could skip the TDD steps and integration verification (agent-browser) since no code changes are being made.' Transcript shows worker invoked 'fullstack-worker' skill but did not write failing tests or launch agent-browser.

summary: PASS. The README.md comprehensively covers all 8 required content areas with accurate, code-verified information.
